verdict.rationale: Grok Build's own MCP docs describe plugging in MCP servers and using their tools. Servers can be added from the CLI over an HTTP transport (`grok mcp add --transport http ...`), and Grok also loads existing configs from `~/.claude.json`, `.cursor/mcp.json` and project `.mcp.json`. Once configured, the servers' tools sit alongside the built-in tools, and `grok inspect` lists discovered MCP servers. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of MCP tool use, and documentation of the other transports (e.g. stdio) and of auth handling.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can plug MCP servers into this product so it can use their tools

citations.quote: MCP servers expose external tools to Grok. Once configured, their tools are available alongside the built-in ones
grok mcp add --transport http linear https://mcp.linear.app/mcp
Grok also loads MCP configurations from `~/.claude.json`, `.cursor/mcp.json`, and project `.mcp.json` files
